exercise.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge Chest Press

reference.title: Dumbbell Glute Bridge Chest Press
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder and elbow; hip extension held)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the hips rise; breathe in at the bottom of the press and out as you press; breathe normally as the hips come down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s bridge up, 1.1 s press, 1.5 s lower

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, then a single-leg bridge. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Lie on the mat, knees bent and feet flat about hip width. A dumbbell in each hand at the chest, upper arms on the floor about 45 degrees from the body.
Squeeze the glutes and drive the hips up until knees, hips and shoulders form one line.
Hold the bridge and press both dumbbells straight up over the shoulders; breathe out.
Lower the dumbbells under control until the upper arms touch the floor; hips stay up.
Lower the hips to the mat, reset, repeat.

mistakes.fix: Keep squeezing the glutes; the knee-hip-shoulder line stays straight.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to lift higher
mistakes.fix: Ribs down; lift with the glutes, not the low back.
Keep the elbows about 45 degrees from the body.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing the elbows off the floor
mistakes.fix: Touch the floor softly with the upper arms and pause.

kinematics.norm: Hips lifted until knees, hips and shoulders line up, knees about 90 degrees (Lehecka 2017 traditional bridge)
About 90 degrees at the top of the bridge (Lehecka 2017)
Floor press range: the elbows stop at the floor (common coaching; Saeterbakken 2011 on chest-press variants)
About 45 degrees from the trunk (common coaching)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #18743, Dumbbell Glute Bridge Chest Press, video (movement reference)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)
Welsch, Bird and Mayhew 2005, electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid muscles during three upper-body lifts (J Strength Cond Res 19(2):449-452)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Get the dumbbells to the chest before lying back, and set them down at your sides at the end.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: lower the bridge slightly and brace.
Shoulder discomfort: tuck the elbows closer to the body.
regressions: Glute bridge with the arms on the floor.
progressions: Alternating presses while holding the bridge.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pressing muscle; the floor stops the elbows at about the back line, so the bottom is a partial range (clinical opinion; Saeterbakken 2011 compared chest-press variants).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straighten the elbows in the press; the floor-limited range keeps the work toward lockout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest in the press (Welsch 2005 measured anterior deltoid in dumbbell presses).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Moves the shoulder blades forward at the top of the press (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Lifts and holds the hips in the bridge while the arms press (Lehecka 2017; Macadam 2019 on glute bridges).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension in the bridge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Keep the knees from drifting apart in the bridge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the knees in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blades set against the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Steadies the shoulder as the dumbbells move (clinical opinion).
